prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: high-resolution transparent source-pose sprite page for Skeleton animation.
Generate newly drawn art, not enlarged original pixels. Layout FOUR columns by TWO rows in exact row-major order, wide 2:1 canvas. Each occupied cell is one complete source pose (or its source death fragments). Keep generous truly transparent gutters and outer margins: whole body, sword, fingers and toes fit in central 75 percent of each cell. Distinct figures must remain spatially separate, no overlaps. Do not add labels or grid.
Input image 1 is APPROVED APPEARANCE ONLY: unarmored human skeleton with warm aged ivory bone, fine cracks, olive-brown patina, hollow dark eye sockets, finely modeled volume. Same lean proportions and exposed ribs/pelvis, bare bony hands and feet. One straight double-edged steel sword, brass/gold crossguard and pommel, dark violet grip. No shield, armor, cloth, glow or new props.
Input image 2 is ORIGINAL POSE AUTHORITY. Follow each guide cell's exact camera/view, shoulder/pelvis turn, skull tilt, joint/foot placement and sword-hand grip, not the master's idle stance. Keep subtle pose differences, do not repeat an idle to fill cells. Original near anatomical sword arm is the hand on screen-left in frontal view; do not swap it when torso rotates. Preserve all source views even when away from camera, and source disarticulation/death fragments. Exactly ONE sword per occupied pose, held by source hand unless the source releases it.

Exact requested mapping (prefix every numbered pose below with skeleton_). Match the corresponding guide cell exactly:
Cell 1: p032: DEATH final frame. A LOW COMPACT HEAP of collapsed skeletal bones, ribs/pelvis/limbs and skull as source; ONE straight sword stands nearly vertically planted within this bone pile, hilt near top, blade down. This pose is the bone pile only, not a standing skeleton. Keep every native detached fragment and relative layout. Do not invent a floor or shadow.
Cell 2: p037: UPPER attack frame2, right-facing narrow body, original sword arm raised overhead with hand at upper right and blade diagonally toward upper LEFT, front knee raised, empty arm back/left. This is a genuine rotated/source side view, not the front attack pose.
Cell 3: p038: UPPER attack frame3, torso twists away from camera showing back/side ribs, skull turned right, original sword hand high to right holding blade up-right, empty arm extends fully toward screen LEFT behind body, legs stepping/crossing.
Cell 4: p039: UPPER attack frame4, strong BACK/THREE-QUARTER AWAY view, original sword arm high to upper right with nearly vertical blade, free arm extends horizontally LEFT, skull seen from rear/side and pelvis twisted. Do not replace with right-facing front view.
Cell 5: p040: UPPER attack frame5, torso starts to untwist toward right/three-quarter view, sword hand forward-right near upper chest and blade diagonally upper LEFT across head region, free arm remains extended LEFT; knees/legs close in stepping stance.
Cell 6: p041: UPPER attack frame6, right-facing recovery, sword hand low-forward right at waist with blade rising upper RIGHT, empty arm bent behind/near torso, stepping feet with one knee/foot lifted. Exact guide wrist and feet.
Cell 7: p048: LOWER attack frame2, sword raised overhead with hilt above skull, blade extends upper LEFT, original near arm raised, empty arm low-forward right, knee lifted. Distinct lower-attack torso tilt, not p043 reused.
Cell 8: p049: LOWER attack frame3, skeleton bends DEEPLY forward/right, skull lowered, original sword hand down in front of hip/knees and blade points steep DOWN-RIGHT far before feet; empty arm flung back/up over curved back to upper right. Preserve low strike and complete blade.
Background MUST be genuine transparent alpha, including holes between ribs and limbs. No haze, gradient, checkerboard, backdrop, floor, cast/contact shadows, text, labels, frames, grid, extra magic or motion trails. Every blade tip and bone inside canvas, no clipped components. Keep modeled bone/metal material finish consistent with approved master, but source pose and view take priority. Render at high resolution with fine shading rather than pixel clusters.
